f218-219.summary: Matignon reports the battery before Monségur: about twelve hundred shots with less effect than hoped, three breaches, Sacramore de Birague badly wounded trying for the lodgement. The army is in need, the forces shrink daily and the pay is what matters most; Mayenne has a fever, but the physicians see no danger.
f218-219.en:
Clear text: "The next day I had it begun at daybreak, [and] it was continued until sunset."

And nearly twelve hundred shots having been fired, they did not however have as much effect as had been promised,
because the wall was also found to be much better than had been thought. Following the design that had been made of
it, three breaches were made, the intention being to lodge on one only of [the three], and to follow up from the two
others so as to see the enemies in their entrenchment[s] [?sa] from behind [?], to prevent them from defending the
said breach, on which, which the par[?], we intended to lodge [ourselves] [? ? who ? u] towards evening. The Sieur
Sacramore de Birague, who was on guard on the side of the said breach, wanted to win the said lodgement, and went
there very courageously and well accompanied;

fr15573-f120.summary: "This prince" is more vexed than ever; the treasurer Bilart wrote that thirty thousand écus in gold have been ready for ten days, the Cardinal of Guise writes that five thousand are coming, but not even a hundred and five thousand would set the army right. Biron cannot be kept; deputies of the army have come; papers of the secretary La Marsilière have fallen into "our" hands.

fr15573-f385.summary: The army in Guyenne is breaking up at the start of winter 1586: not a thousand foot left, men asking for leave, no powder. The letter asks what to do with the regiments and the foreigners over the winter, and names the landsknechts from Champagne, a company of light horse, Monsieur d'Halincourt, Monsieur de Matignon and La Roche.
